During the crime data analysis, the project primarily focused on the after-before ratio of ND crime ratios, which is the ratio between the ND crime ratio after the LED conversion and the ND crime ratio before LED conversion. Using the after-before ratio of the ND ratios for the two cities, the project team was able to compare the ND ratios between the two cities while taking into consideration potential crime changes after the LED conversion while minimizing the number of regression models needed. Note that the analysis determined nighttime crimes based 70 on the crime reporting time instead of the crime time. This was because many of the crime records did not include a crime time due to the fact that the actual times when many crimes took place were not known. The crime data analysis relied on both GLM regression and t-tests. The project team analyzed the nighttime crime data for the following scenarios: • All nighttime crimes: after-before ratio of ND crime ratios comparing Cambridge and Somerville (1), • Nighttime crimes after midnight: after-before ratio of ND crime ratios comparing Cambridge (for C2 roadways) and Somerville (for HPMS roadways) (2), • Nighttime crimes after 10:00 p.m., after-before ND crime ratio comparing between Cambridge (C2 roadways) and Somerville (HPMS roadways) (3), and • Nighttime crimes after 8:00 p.m., after-before ND crime ratio comparing between Cambridge (C3 roadways) and Somerville (local streets) (4). During the crime data analysis, the project team developed models for two scenarios: the after- before LED conversion ratio of ND crime ratios comparison between Cambridge and Somerville for all nighttime crimes and by dimming schedule, and the analysis of the ND crime ratios by lighting levels. Recall that the after-before ratio of ND crime ratios was computed as the ratio of the ND crime ratios after and before the LED conversion. The first scenario used both GLM and t-tests in an effort to capture all potential significant differences. The second scenario used GLM in an effort to identify significant correlations between lighting levels and ND crime ratios by roadway types and dimming schedule. The analysis developed models separately for four lighting measures similar to the crash analysis: average horizontal illuminance, minimum horizontal illuminance, maximum horizontal illuminance, and horizontal illuminance standard deviation. 4.2.2.1 Comparing After-Before Ratios of ND Crime Ratios by Dimming Schedule Table 30 and Table 31 list the GLM and t-test results comparing Cambridge and Somerville ND crime ratio ratios, respectively. As both tests indicated, none of the after-before crime ratios between the two cities when analyzing the crime data by dimming schedules were significant at a 0.05 level of significance. When testing all ND crime ratios regardless of roadway types and nighttime periods, however, both tests indicated that the after-before ratio for Cambridge was significantly lower than that for Somerville.
